All dashboard API endpoints require platformAdminRoute middleware
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: COMPLETE. server/routes-security-dashboard.ts with admin-only endpoints. Security event aggregation from threat detection, auth hardening, exfiltration guard, and CORS violations.

userStories.title: Internal penetration testing harness using OWASP methodology
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an internal security testing harness that runs Shannon-style attack patterns against our own platform so that we find vulnerabilities before external tools do.
acceptanceCriteria: Create scripts/pentest/ directory with modular test scripts following OWASP Testing Guide categories

Create scripts/pentest/auth-tests.ts: brute force login, credential stuffing with common passwords, session fixation, JWT manipulation (algorithm confusion, expired token replay, signature stripping), MFA bypass attempts, password reset flow abuse

Create scripts/pentest/injection-tests.ts: SQL injection payloads on all form fields and query params, XSS payloads (reflected, stored, DOM-based) on all text input endpoints, command injection payloads on any endpoint that processes filenames or URLs, SSRF payloads on webhook/integration endpoints

Create scripts/pentest/authz-tests.ts: IDOR testing (accessing other users' resources by ID manipulation), tenant isolation testing (cross-tenant data access), privilege escalation (lower role accessing admin endpoints), horizontal privilege escalation (user A accessing user B's data)
Create scripts/pentest/config.ts for target configuration: base URL, test credentials per role level, tenant IDs for cross-tenant testing, output directory for reports
Create scripts/pentest/reporter.ts generating HTML report with: findings by severity, proof of concept for each finding, remediation recommendations, OWASP category mapping
Add npm script test:pentest that runs the full internal pentest suite against a running instance
Tests should verify defenses hold (expect 403/429 responses, not 200s with data)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: COMPLETE. Created full pentest harness at scripts/pentest/: auth-tests.ts (6 tests: brute force, credential stuffing, JWT manipulation, session fixation, password reset abuse, MFA bypass), injection-tests.ts (7 tests: SQL injection on search/form fields, reflected XSS, stored XSS, command injection, SSRF, null byte injection), authz-tests.ts (6 tests: IDOR, cross-tenant header tampering, vertical privilege escalation, HTTP method override, path traversal, unauthenticated API access), config.ts (target configuration), reporter.ts (HTML+JSON report with OWASP mapping), index.ts (main runner). npm script test:pentest added. Tests verify defenses hold (expect 403/429, not 200s). Build passes.

userStories.title: Session security hardening - token rotation, device binding, and replay prevention
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need hardened session management so that AI pentest tools cannot replay, fixate, or hijack user sessions even if they obtain a token.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement JWT refresh token rotation: each refresh grants a new refresh token and invalidates the previous one, detect and revoke entire token family if a previously-used refresh token is replayed (indicates theft)
Add device fingerprint binding to sessions: hash of User-Agent + Accept-Language + screen resolution (from client) stored with session, flag sessions where fingerprint changes mid-session
Implement session invalidation on privilege change: when user role changes, all existing sessions are invalidated requiring re-authentication
Add /api/auth/sessions endpoint for users to view and revoke their active sessions (device, location, last active)
Store session metadata in security_sessions table: device fingerprint, IP address, created_at, last_active_at, is_suspicious flag
Create server/tests/unit/session-hardening.test.ts covering: token rotation works, replay detection triggers revocation, fingerprint mismatch flagged, privilege change invalidates sessions
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: COMPLETE. server/middleware/session-hardening.ts with device fingerprinting, refresh token rotation with replay detection, token family revocation, session invalidation on role changes. Tests in server/tests/unit/session-hardening.test.ts.

userStories.title: Request fingerprinting and bot detection middleware
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need automated bot and tool detection so that AI pentest reconnaissance tools (Nmap, WhatWeb, Subfinder, headless browsers) are identified and their requests flagged before they begin exploitation.
acceptanceCriteria: Create server/middleware/bot-detection.ts that analyzes request characteristics: User-Agent string patterns matching known security tools (nmap, nikto, sqlmap, whatweb, schemathesis, nuclei, burpsuite, zap), headless browser indicators (missing Accept-Language, navigator.webdriver, HeadlessChrome UA), TLS fingerprinting anomalies via JA3/JA4 hash comparison (if available from reverse proxy headers)

Implement request cadence analysis: perfectly uniform request intervals indicate automation (humans have jitter), missing standard browser headers (Accept, Accept-Encoding, Cache-Control) on web requests
Create a bot score (0-100) that feeds into the threat detection service (SEC-008)
Add configurable response for detected bots: allow (log only), challenge (CAPTCHA/JS challenge), throttle (artificial delay), block (403)
Create server/config/bot-signatures.ts with updatable list of known tool signatures and detection patterns
Do NOT block legitimate bots (Googlebot, etc.) - maintain an allowlist for verified crawler User-Agents with reverse DNS verification
Create server/tests/unit/bot-detection.test.ts covering: normal browser passes, known tool UA detected, headless browser detected, legitimate crawler allowed, missing headers flagged
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: COMPLETE. server/middleware/bot-detection.ts with bot scoring (0-100). server/config/bot-signatures.ts with security tool patterns (nmap, sqlmap, burpsuite, etc). Legitimate crawler allowlist (Googlebot, Bingbot). Tests in server/tests/unit/bot-detection.test.ts.

userStories.title: Error message sanitization and information leakage prevention

Ensure 404 responses don't enumerate valid vs invalid routes (consistent response format for all unmatched routes)
Audit all catch blocks in route files: replace any res.status(500).json({ error: err.message }) with sanitized generic messages in production
Create server/tests/unit/error-sanitization.test.ts: database errors return generic message, file path errors scrubbed, stack traces removed in production mode, 404s are consistent format

userStories.notes: COMPLETE. server/utils/error-sanitizer.ts scrubs 11+ categories of sensitive info (PG details, file paths, IPs, SQL, stack traces). userStories.title: Add bulk operations toolbar with multi-select to all list pages

userStories.title: Fix critical SQL injection in storage.ts getBusinessRecords via string interpolation
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need the SQL injection vulnerability in storage.ts getBusinessRecords() fixed because user-controlled parameters (recordType, status, search, limit) are directly interpolated into raw SQL strings via template literals and sql.raw(), allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace string interpolation in WHERE clause construction (lines 2733-2746) with Drizzle ORM parameterized queries
Replace sql.raw(whereClause) with proper Drizzle where() conditions using eq(), like(), and(), or()
Replace sql.raw(limitClause) with Drizzle .limit() method
All parameters (tenantId, recordType, status, search, limit) use parameterized queries only
Search functionality uses parameterized LIKE with sql`...${searchTerm}...` not string interpolation
No sql.raw() calls remain in getBusinessRecords()
Existing business records functionality works identically
Typecheck passes: npm run check

userStories.title: Fix edge-function proxy to handle multipart bodies and binary responses
userStories.description: Architectural fix: server/middleware/edge-function-proxy.ts currently does JSON.stringify(req.body) which corrupts multipart/form-data uploads (CSV imports), and uses await response.text() which corrupts binary responses (PDFs, ZIP downloads). This blocks any /import or /pdf endpoint from being safely proxied.

Detect Content-Type on the edge response: if not JSON-ish (text/*, application/json), use response.arrayBuffer() and res.end(Buffer.from(buf)) to preserve binary
Add unit test for multipart pass-through (mock edge function returning 200, verify boundary preserved)
Add unit test for binary response (mock edge function returning a PNG, verify byte-equal pass-through)

userStories.description: supabase/functions/server.ts:108 strips the function name from the URL before dispatching to the handler (newUrl.pathname = '/' + pathParts.slice(1).join('/')). Each table also has created_at, updated_at (timestamptz), created_by_user_id (FK users)
Indices on hot paths: blog_posts(tenant_id, status, published_at), blog_keywords(tenant_id, cluster_id), blog_distributions(post_id, platform), blog_refresh_queue(tenant_id, scheduled_at)
RLS policies on every blog_* table enforce tenant_id matches the JWT app_metadata.tenantId claim — matches existing Printyx RLS pattern
Schema re-exported from shared/schema.ts so drizzle-kit picks it up
npm run db:generate produces a clean migration in drizzle/migrations/
Migration applies cleanly with npm run db:migrate against a clean dev DB
Typecheck passes: npm run check

userStories.title: Auth + RBAC: gate blog access via Printyx Supabase auth and platform roles
userStories.description: As a platform admin, I need every blog endpoint and UI route gated to the right Printyx role so editorial workflow respects existing permissions without inventing a parallel auth system.
acceptanceCriteria: New blog permissions added to RBAC seed: blog.post.view, blog.post.edit, blog.post.publish, blog.post.delete, blog.brand_voice.edit, blog.style_guide.edit, blog.distribution.publish, blog.analytics.view, blog.refresh.manage, blog.agent.toggle
Default grants — Platform Admin: all blog.* permissions; Company Admin: view + edit + publish + analytics within their tenant; all other roles: none in v1
Every blog edge function authenticates via supabase.auth.getUser(jwt), pulls tenantId from app_metadata, and checks the relevant blog.* permission before performing any work
Permission checks are server-side; UI gating in client/src/pages/platform-admin/blog/* is convenience only
Every mutating action writes a row to blog_audit_log (action, actor_user_id, target_type, target_id, before_jsonb, after_jsonb, tenant_id, created_at)
No invite flow is needed in v1 — workspace membership maps 1:1 to existing Printyx role assignment
Integration test: a non-platform-admin user calling a blog endpoint receives 403
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Source PRD: blog-system-prd.json US-BLOG-003 (adapted to Printyx auth). The original PRD's pluggable auth + invite flow is replaced by Printyx's existing Supabase Auth + tenant role assignment.

userStories.title: Workspace settings: brand voice profile
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a per-workspace brand voice so every AI-generated draft matches our tone without re-prompting each time.
acceptanceCriteria: brand_voices table fields: workspace_id, name, tone (free text), banned_phrases (text[]), preferred_phrases (text[]), reading_level_target (enum: grade-6 to grade-14), persona_description, sample_corpus (text — paste-in examples), pov (first/second/third person), voice_attributes (jsonb: humor, formality, technicality on 1-5 scale)
Admin UI form to create/edit brand voice with live preview using a fixed sample paragraph rewritten in the configured voice
Brand voice ID can be attached to posts, briefs, and distribution variants
Default brand voice per workspace; multiple voices supported (e.g., 'corporate blog' vs 'founder POV')
Brand voice serializes to a system-prompt fragment used by every AI step
userStories.notes: Sample corpus is the highest-signal field — keep the textarea generous (10k chars).

userStories.title: Style guide linter (prose-level rules)
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a style guide that flags violations during writing so authors stay on-brand without manual review of every comma.
acceptanceCriteria: style_guides table per workspace: rules (jsonb array of {pattern, severity, message, replacement?})
Built-in rule packs: AP, Chicago, MLA, plain-language, inclusive-language
Custom rules: regex or substring with severity (error/warn/info)
Linter runs in editor in real time; underlines violations with hover-to-explain
Linter also runs server-side on save and blocks publish if any 'error'-severity rules fail (unless overridden by editor+ role)
userStories.notes: Use a worker-thread or web worker so linting doesn't block typing on long posts.

userStories.title: CMS adapter interface + WordPress and Ghost adapters (v1 set)
userStories.description: As a developer publishing blog posts to Printyx's marketing site (and later to other CMS targets), I want a stable adapter interface so v1 can ship WordPress + Ghost and phase 2 can add Webflow + custom-REST + native-render without changing call sites.

Adapter selection per tenant via cms_adapter (enum: wordpress|ghost) and cms_config (jsonb, encrypted at column level via Printyx credential vault) on a new blog_cms_targets table
Markdown-to-CMS transform layer normalizes output for each CMS's quirks (Gutenberg blocks for WP, mobiledoc/Lexical for Ghost)
Shared contract test suite asserts every adapter satisfies the same behavioral spec
Phase 2 adapters (Webflow, custom-REST, native-render) are explicitly out of scope for this story — capture in notes as follow-up
Never log decrypted CMS credentials
Typecheck passes: npm run check

userStories.title: Rich-text editor with Markdown parity
userStories.description: As a writer, I want a powerful editor that round-trips between Markdown and rich text so I can paste, draft fast, and preserve structure.
acceptanceCriteria: TipTap (or Lexical) with extensions: headings, lists, blockquotes, code blocks (syntax highlighted), tables, images with alt text, links with title, footnotes, callouts/admonitions
Markdown import: paste Markdown and it converts to rich nodes
Markdown export: every post stores canonical Markdown in posts.body_markdown alongside posts.body_html
Slash-command menu (/) for inserting blocks
Inline AI toolbar: highlight text → 'rewrite shorter / expand / change tone / cite source'
Autosave to post_revisions every 10s of inactivity
userStories.notes: Markdown as source of truth simplifies migrations and avoids editor-lock-in. Implemented: TipTap with StarterKit + CodeBlockLowlight (syntax-highlighted via lowlight common langs + github-dark theme) + Table/Row/Cell/Header (resizable, header row) + Link + Image + Placeholder + Typography + custom SlashCommand extension (via @tiptap/suggestion + tippy.js, 10 commands: H1/H2/H3, bullet/numbered list, quote, code, table, divider, image). Markdown round-trip uses marked (gfm:true) + turndown with turndown-plugin-gfm (tables + strikethrough) and a custom rule that preserves language tags on fenced code blocks (```ts). Autosave wired by parent BlogPostEditor → POST /blog-post-revisions (US-BLOG-009). Inline AI rewrite toolbar (AC #5) deferred to a future iteration as US-BLOG-032 — depends on _shared/blog/llm.ts helper not yet built. Footnotes + callouts (AC #1 tail) deferred as separate stories — both require custom node extensions.

userStories.title: Version history with diff and restore
userStories.description: As an editor, I want to see every revision of a post so I can recover from mistakes and review changes.
acceptanceCriteria: post_revisions table: post_id, author_id, body_markdown, title, meta_title, meta_description, created_at
Admin UI history panel shows revision list with author + timestamp
Side-by-side diff view (markdown-aware) between any two revisions
One-click restore creates a new revision rather than overwriting
Revisions retained for 90 days minimum; configurable per workspace
userStories.notes: Diff at the markdown level; HTML diffs are noisy. Implemented: blog-post-revisions edge function (list/get/create/restore with dedup + audit), 10s autosave from BlogPostEditor (revision_source='manual'), BlogPostHistory page with diffLines from npm 'diff' package + restore alert dialog, retention via blog_agent_settings.revision_retention_days (default 90, range 7-730) and POST /blog-post-revisions/cleanup which preserves the latest revision per post.

userStories.title: Asset library: images, quotes, data, expert contacts
userStories.description: As an editor, I want a single place to manage reusable assets so research and visuals are findable across posts.
acceptanceCriteria: Assets table with type enum: image, quote, data_table, expert_contact, link, file
Upload to S3-compatible storage (Cloudflare R2 / Supabase Storage adapter)
Image assets: auto-generate thumbnails, extract EXIF, store dimensions, original filename, alt text, license/source
Quote assets: text, attributed_to, source_url, retrieved_at, license
Data table assets: csv upload → preview, column types, optional chart preview
Expert contact assets: name, expertise tags, email/contact, prior quotes given, response rate
Search across assets by tag, type, text
userStories.notes: License/source on every asset is non-negotiable for E-E-A-T and legal safety. Implemented: Supabase Storage bucket 'blog-assets' (25 MB cap, image+csv+pdf+json+text mime allowlist) provisioned via _backfill_blog_assets_bucket.sql. blog-assets edge function with list/get/create/patch/delete + POST /upload-url that issues a signed upload URL to a tenant-scoped path '<tenant_id>/<uuid>-<filename>' (refuses cross-tenant storage paths on create). Library page at /platform-admin/blog/assets with type filter, free-text search across title/description/attribution, type-colored card grid, soft delete with confirm. Upload modal with type-specific forms (image: alt text required; quote: text + attribution/source URL; expert_contact: name/title/org/contact/expertise tags). Image picker dialog integrated into BlogEditor — replaces the prior window.prompt flow on both the toolbar Image button and the slash-menu Image entry; supports inline 'upload new' and auto-selects the freshly uploaded asset. Deferred: thumbnail generation, EXIF extraction, CSV preview/column-typing, expert-contact response-rate tracking, link asset type — each a follow-up since each is its own non-trivial pipeline. Schema's enum is {image, quote, data, expert_contact, file}; AC's 'data_table' and 'link' types not added to enum since (a) 'data' covers data tables and (b) link assets are already representable as URLs in body markdown without their own row.

userStories.title: Audit log for every mutating action
userStories.description: As a workspace owner, I want a tamper-evident audit log so I can investigate incidents and prove compliance.
acceptanceCriteria: audit_log table: workspace_id, actor_user_id, action (string), target_type, target_id, before (jsonb), after (jsonb), ip, user_agent, created_at
Middleware logs every POST/PATCH/DELETE on the API
Admin UI: audit log viewer with filters (actor, action, date range)
Logs retained 1 year minimum; configurable
Append-only — no UPDATE or DELETE permission on audit_log via RLS
userStories.notes: Consider periodic export to immutable storage (S3 with object lock) for tamper-evidence.

userStories.title: Background job queue with retries and observability
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a reliable job system so AI calls, syndication, and analytics ingest can run async with backoff.
acceptanceCriteria: pg-boss (preferred — uses Postgres) or BullMQ adapter
Job types defined as TypeScript discriminated unions; handlers in apps/worker
Default policy: exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 30m, 2h), max 5 attempts
Job dashboard in admin UI: pending, active, failed, completed counts; retry / cancel buttons
Failed jobs surface in audit_log with full error stack
Idempotency keys on every job to prevent duplicate work
userStories.notes: pg-boss avoids a Redis dependency for small deployments. Implemented as a lightweight Postgres-native queue (no pg-boss/BullMQ since the deploy has no always-on Node worker — everything is Deno edge functions). Built: blog_jobs table (status/priority/scheduled_at/attempts/max_attempts/last_error/result/idempotency_key/locked_until/locked_by), POST /blog-jobs (enqueue with idempotency dedup), GET /blog-jobs/stats (queued/active/failed/completed/cancelled counts), GET /blog-jobs?status&type, POST /blog-jobs/:id/retry, POST /blog-jobs/:id/cancel, POST /blog-jobs/run-due (cron entry point — claims due jobs with two-step UPDATE ... WHERE status='queued' AND id IN(...) approximating SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, runs in-process, applies 1m/5m/30m/2h exponential backoff, marks final fail after max_attempts). Built-in handlers: noop (smoke test) + retention_cleanup (invokes US-BLOG-009 cleanup logic). Dashboard at /platform-admin/blog/settings/jobs with status cards (5s polling), filterable jobs table, retry/cancel actions, expandable row showing payload/result/stack. Every state transition writes a blog_audit_log row (enqueue, complete, fail_retry, fail_permanent, retry, cancel). External cron wiring (k8s CronJob → POST /blog-jobs/run-due) is operations-side, not in this story.

userStories.title: Keyword research adapter interface + DataForSEO reference adapter
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want keyword data (volume, difficulty, CPC, trend) so I can prioritize topics with measurable demand.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/core/keyword-adapter.ts: searchVolume, keywordDifficulty, relatedKeywords, autocomplete, trend12mo
Adapters: dataforseo (reference), ahrefs, semrush, google-keyword-planner — all implementing the same interface
Workspace setting: which adapter + API credentials (encrypted)
Keyword cache table to avoid re-querying within TTL (default 30 days)
Bulk lookup endpoint: paste a list of seed keywords → returns enriched data
Cost tracking: every adapter call logs estimated cost in cents to ai_costs table
userStories.notes: Cost tracking matters — keyword APIs are metered and bills sneak up fast.

userStories.title: Search intent classifier
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want every keyword classified by intent so I plan the right content format.
acceptanceCriteria: Classifier tags each keyword: informational, commercial-investigation, transactional, navigational, with confidence score
Implementation: LLM prompt that takes keyword + top 10 SERP titles/snippets and returns intent + reasoning
Bulk classify on keyword import; cached on keywords.intent column
Admin UI: filter keyword list by intent; intent shown as colored chip
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. Shared classifier supabase/functions/_shared/blog/keyword/intent-classifier.ts (Claude, temp 0, JSON-only prompt, graceful degrade on parse failure, 0-100/0-1 confidence coercion, synonym tolerance). New edge function supabase/functions/blog-keywords/index.ts: GET / (intent/search/source_type/cluster_id/unclassified filters + paging + tenant-wide intent_counts), POST /classify (bulk; pulls top-10 organic titles+snippets from latest blog_serp_snapshots per keyword when use_serp, caches intent on blog_keywords.intent, stores confidence/reasoning/serp_informed/classified_at in raw_data.intent_meta, audit-logged), PATCH /:id manual override (audit-logged). Intent stored as 4 short canonical values (commercial = PRD commercial-investigation, varchar(20) safe). Frontend client/src/pages/platform-admin/blog/BlogKeywords.tsx: filterable table, colored intent chips, confidence %, SERP-informed dot, one-click Classify unclassified, per-row reclassify + manual-override select. Wired into App.tsx route /platform-admin/blog/keywords and BlogShell nav (g k). SCOPE: 'classify on keyword import' delivered as a bulk endpoint + one-click UI rather than an auto-trigger inside the PAA miner hot path (auto per-keyword LLM calls during a mine of hundreds of PAA rows would be cost/latency-prohibitive). No DB migration: reused existing raw_data jsonb. tsc clean for new files, vite build green (BlogKeywords lazy-chunked 6.86 kB).

userStories.title: SERP analyzer for any keyword
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want to see what currently ranks so I can match or exceed the bar.
acceptanceCriteria: SERP fetcher (DataForSEO or scraping adapter) returns top 20 organic results + SERP features (PAA, featured snippet, knowledge panel, video, image pack, local pack)
For each result: URL, title, meta description, domain, estimated DA, word count (fetched + parsed), heading structure (H2/H3)
Aggregated metrics: median word count, common headings, common entities, dominant content type (listicle/guide/comparison/etc.)
Stored in serp_snapshots table with fetched_at timestamp; re-fetch on demand or weekly
Admin UI: SERP analyzer view with sortable table + aggregate summary card
userStories.notes: Word count parsing must handle paywalls and JS-rendered content gracefully — fall back to meta description length when blocked. Implemented: KeywordAdapter contract extended with optional fetchSerp(creds, keyword, opts) returning {organic, features, cost}. DataForSEO impl wraps POST /v3/serp/google/organic/live/advanced and maps items to organic (rank/url/title/description/domain), featured_snippet, paa (with expanded answers), knowledge_panel, has_video_pack/image_pack/local_pack. blog_serp_snapshots table caches per (tenant, keyword, location_code, language_code, fetched_at). blog-serp edge function: POST /blog-serp/fetch (fetches, does best-effort per-URL parse with 3s timeout + 6 concurrency, falls back to snippet word-count when blocked), GET /blog-serp (list summaries), GET /blog-serp/:id (full), DELETE /blog-serp/:id. Aggregates computed at insert time: median/mean word count, common H2s (top 5, normalized + folded, requires count>=2), dominant_content_type heuristic (listicle/how_to/comparison/guide/review based on title patterns; nulls when no clear winner). Admin UI at /platform-admin/blog/serp with keyword + location + language input, recent snapshots sidebar, aggregate summary card, feature chips, sortable organic table (rank/word_count/domain), PAA section. New blog sub-nav entry 'SERP' (g e shortcut). Deferred: estimated DA (would need a separate DA lookup adapter — Moz / Ahrefs DR), common entities (NLP — could be heuristic noun-phrase extraction or LLM-driven later), automatic weekly re-fetch (will hook into US-BLOG-012 job queue once cron is wired).

userStories.title: People Also Ask + autocomplete miner
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want every related question surfaced so my content covers the actual user journey.
acceptanceCriteria: Recursive PAA crawler: fetch PAA for seed keyword, then for each PAA result, fetch its PAA (depth 2 default, configurable up to 4)
Google autocomplete fetcher: A-Z + 0-9 prefix expansion for seed keyword
Results stored in keywords table with source = 'paa' or 'autocomplete' and parent keyword reference
Deduplication and grouping by lexical similarity
Admin UI: tree view of PAA chains; click to add to brief
userStories.notes: Respect rate limits — back off aggressively on 429s. Implemented: extended blog_keywords with source_type, parent_keyword_id (self-FK), parent_question, mining_depth columns (backfill SQL idempotent). blog-paa-miner edge function: POST /mine (BFS over PAA up to depth 4, persists each Q with parent link; concurrent autocomplete fan-out across A-Z + 0-9 prefixes — 36 calls/seed when enabled; both passes share a normalized-keyword dedup set so the same string never round-trips twice), GET /tree?keyword= (walks descendants via parent_keyword_id, splits into PAA chain + flat autocomplete list, capped at 2000 nodes), DELETE /clear?keyword= (removes descendants only, preserves seed). Uses the existing tenant DataForSEO target. Adapter calls wrapped in retryOn429 (single 2-second pause). UI at /platform-admin/blog/paa with keyword + depth + location/language + toggles for PAA and autocomplete, expandable tree view (chevron toggles, ChildrenMap rendered recursively), copy-on-click + 'Copy all PAA' bulk export, autocomplete shown as wrap-friendly chip cloud, 'Clear run' destructive action. New blog sub-nav 'PAA' (g q shortcut). Dedup is exact normalized-string match (lowercase + alphanumeric); near-duplicate clustering by Levenshtein/Jaro deferred — current dedup is enough for v1 since DataForSEO normalizes most rephrasings.

userStories.title: Forum / community question miner (Reddit, Quora, Stack Exchange)

userStories.title: Competitor content gap analysis
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want to see keywords competitors rank for that we don't so I can prioritize quick wins.
acceptanceCriteria: Workspace setting: competitor_domains (text[])
Job fetches each competitor's ranked keywords from the keyword adapter
Diff view: keywords competitors rank in top 10 for, where our domain ranks >20 or not at all
Filter by intent, volume, difficulty
One-click 'Create cluster from gap' adds the keyword group to keyword_clusters with source = 'gap_analysis'
Re-run on schedule (weekly default)
userStories.notes: Surface 'easy wins' first: keywords where competitors rank but their content is shallow. Implemented: extended blog_agent_settings with own_domain (varchar) + competitor_domains (text[]). New blog_competitor_keywords table (id/tenant_id/domain/is_own/keyword/rank/search_volume/keyword_difficulty/cpc/intent/source_adapter/raw_data/fetched_at) with UNIQUE(tenant_id, domain, keyword) so each scan replaces prior rows for that domain. KeywordAdapter contract extended with optional rankedKeywords(creds, domain, opts). DataForSEO impl wraps /v3/dataforseo_labs/google/ranked_keywords/live with server-side max_rank filter + cleanDomain helper. blog-competitor-gap edge function: GET/PATCH /settings (own + competitor domain config — also normalizes domains with cleanDomain), POST /scan (deletes prior rows per domain then inserts in 500-row batches, captures partial failures per-domain), GET /gaps (in-process diff: builds a keyword → {own_rank, competitor_ranks{}} map, applies intent/min_volume/max_difficulty/min_competitors/own_min_rank filters, computes easy_win_score = volume/max(1,difficulty)*10 when best competitor is top-5; sorts by easy_win then volume desc), POST /create-cluster (creates a blog_keyword_clusters row + reassigns or inserts blog_keywords rows with cluster_id + source_type='gap_analysis' + folded competitor metrics; existing rows get re-linked, new ones get created with metric data pulled from the most recent competitor row). UI at /platform-admin/blog/competitor-gap with domain settings card (chip-style competitor editor + Add/Enter-to-commit), Save + Scan buttons, gap table with multi-select + filters + per-competitor rank columns + trophy badge for best_competitor_rank <=3 + Zap badge for easy_win_score, Create cluster dialog, Copy CSV export. New blog sub-nav 'Gaps' (g g shortcut). Weekly schedule (AC #6) deferred — slots cleanly into US-BLOG-012 job queue as a 'competitor_gap_scan' handler once cron is wired.

userStories.title: Self-critiquing agent loop for draft quality

acceptanceCriteria: Pipeline: generator → critic (separate prompt with critique rubric) → reviser → critic → reviser, max 3 iterations

userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. Built on the US-BLOG-031 draft pipeline. runCritiqueLoop() in supabase/functions/blog-draft/index.ts: generator → critic → reviser → critic … max 3 iterations, stops early when the critic returns verdict 'ok' or zero issues. CRITIC_SYSTEM scores the exact rubric (clarity, originality, evidence, voice_match, seo_compliance, factual_grounding, structural_balance, 0-10) + actionable issues[] + verdict; REVISER_SYSTEM fixes the listed issues while preserving structure/citations/brand voice. Every iteration (incl. the pre-critique initial draft) is persisted to blog_post_revisions (revision_source ai_draft/ai_rewrite, diff_summary = critic feedback, shared agent_run_id, auto-incremented revision_number) so the feedback log is viewable in the existing Post History UI alongside the final draft (AC5). Per-tenant toggle: new blog_agent_settings.critique_loop_enabled (default false — costs more tokens), idempotent migration drizzle/migrations/_backfill_blog_critique_loop.sql, exposed in blog-agents settingsPatchSchema and as a Switch card in BlogSettings. Loop is gated on that flag, only runs inside /blog-draft/generate. Cost accumulated into blog_posts.ai_assistance_meta {steps_used:[draft_generator,critique_loop], cost_usd, critique_iterations, critique_log[]}; critique_log also returned in the API response. tsc clean for touched files (unrelated pre-existing BlogSettings* sibling errors untouched), vite build green. All 6 AC met. Note honored: the critic prompt is isolated + the single highest-leverage tuning point.

userStories.title: Auto-refresh agent — fully autonomous SERP-decay-triggered re-editing
userStories.description: As a platform admin, I want the auto-refresh agent to detect SERP decay and re-edit posts WITHOUT human review (per scope decision 5D), with every change captured in the audit log and revertable, so content stays competitive without operator overhead.
acceptanceCriteria: Auto-refresh agent runs on a schedule (cron via Supabase scheduled functions) and via blog_refresh_queue triggers

For each candidate post, the agent: (1) re-runs SERP analysis, (2) diffs against the prior SERP snapshot, (3) generates revised sections, (4) commits a new revision to blog_post_revisions with revision_source="auto_refresh_agent", (5) re-publishes via the configured CMS adapter, (6) writes a blog_audit_log entry summarizing what changed and why
No human-approval step in the default path; admin can opt back into manual review per-tenant via a flag on a new blog_agent_settings row (auto_refresh_requires_review boolean, default false)

Hard guardrails: agent will NOT auto-publish if (a) the predicted change exceeds N% of the post body (configurable, default 40%), (b) the SEO score would drop, or (c) brand-voice or style-guide violations are introduced — these cases land in a review queue surfaced on the Refresh page
Every auto-refresh run respects the global agent kill switch (US-BLOG-086) — if paused, run is skipped and a blog_audit_log entry records the skip
Cost-per-run captured in the AI cost dashboard (US-BLOG-079)
Integration test: simulate SERP decay → assert revision created → assert CMS adapter called → assert audit log entry exists
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Source PRD: blog-system-prd.json US-BLOG-066 (elevated from "proposed edits" to "autonomous re-editing" per scope decision 5D). userStories.title: Harden token refresh (single-flight, propagate failure, clear keychain on terminal 401)
userStories.description: As a user, concurrent 401s can wedge auth or leave stale tokens that fail forever, because the manual isRefreshingToken flag + continuation array doesn't fan out refresh failures and a terminal refresh failure never clears the keychain.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the isRefreshingToken flag + pendingRequests continuation array (APIClient.swift:482-496) with a single shared Task<Void,Error> that concurrent callers await
Waiters are resumed with the refresh result; on refresh failure they throw unauthorized rather than retrying with a cleared token
On terminal 401 (retry still 401), call keychain.clearAll() and drive a deterministic logout (APIClient.swift:281-294)
No second refresh can start while waiters from the first wave are mid-retry
Extend APIClientTests/AuthManagerTests with a concurrent-401 scenario

userStories.notes: Networking audit C1 + security audit M2. Risk: auth wedging and confusing 401 storms instead of a clean logout.

userStories.title: Offline write-queue correctness — dedup, idempotency, ordering, no silent data loss
userStories.description: As a field rep on flaky cellular, the offline write queue can create duplicate records, replay mutations out of order, and silently drop a write after 5 attempts even though I saw a success toast.
acceptanceCriteria: Dedup on a content hash (method+path+body) at enqueue so a double-tap offline doesn't queue two writes (OfflineWriteQueue.swift:56-87; APIClient.swift:363 currently mints a fresh UUID per enqueue)
Add a client-generated idempotency key header so replayed POSTs (create activity, attachment) are server-side idempotent
Preserve ordering: stop the flush loop on first failure (or track dependencies) so a failed create can't be overtaken by a dependent write (OfflineWriteQueue.swift flush, APIClient.swift:356-402)
A write dropped after max attempts surfaces to the user / is logged, never silently discarded; the success toast only fires on confirmed enqueue+eventual send
Extend OfflineWriteQueueTests for dedup, ordering-on-partial-failure, and drop-notification
ios xcodebuild test passes
userStories.notes: Networking audit C2. Multi-tenant CRM data corruption risk. Photo uploads (TicketPhotoPickerSheet) ride this queue.

Verify NSMicrophoneUsageDescription + NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription are present (they are) so dictation doesn't crash on first use

userStories.title: Remove hardcoded debug Supabase anon JWT; inject via xcconfig and rotate

acceptanceCriteria: Remove the literal debugSupabaseAnonKey from AppConfig.swift:26

userStories.title: Keychain accessibility hardening + biometric-gated token release
userStories.description: As a security engineer, refresh/access tokens are readable while the device is locked and the biometric lock only gates the UI (not the keychain), so a locked-but-powered stolen device is more exposed than necessary.
acceptanceCriteria: Store accessToken/refreshToken (and ideally all auth items) with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly instead of AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly (KeychainManager.swift:123)

Gate token *release* behind a SecAccessControl (.biometryCurrentSet / .userPresence) so the keychain itself enforces presence, not just the SwiftUI isLocked swap (BiometricLockManager / RootView.swift:23-30)
Add basic jailbreak heuristics as defense-in-depth
Auth/login/refresh flows still work end-to-end after the accessibility change
ios xcodebuild test passes
userStories.notes: Security audit H1/H3. No background path reads tokens while locked, so WhenUnlocked is safe.

userStories.title: Tenant-context integrity + reliable server-side logout
userStories.description: As a security engineer, the client sends a client-controlled x-tenant-id derived from a stale keychain value, and logout fires the server revoke best-effort without awaiting, so a 'logged out' refresh token can remain valid.
acceptanceCriteria: Re-derive x-tenant-id from the freshly decoded access-token claim on each request/refresh rather than a stale keychain value (APIClient.swift:467-470; AuthManager.swift:173 currently falls back to old keychain on refresh)
Confirm (and document) that edge functions derive tenant from the verified JWT claim and reject/ignore a mismatched x-tenant-id header — the client header must not be a trust boundary

logout() awaits the /auth/v1/logout revoke and surfaces failure; queue the revoke for retry on next launch if it fails (AuthManager.swift:136-146; note the offline queue excludes /auth/* at APIEndpoint.swift:39)

userStories.title: Harden the response cache (SHA-256 keys + integrity, invalidation on mutation, TTL)
userStories.description: As a performance/security engineer, the persistent cache keys list payloads with a 64-bit FNV hash (cross-tenant collision risk), never invalidates on mutation (ghost/stale data offline), and double-caches every GET alongside URLCache.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the 64-bit FNV-1a filename with SHA-256 of (tenantId|path?query) and store the plaintext key inside the blob to verify on read (PersistentResponseCache.swift:31-39)

Add shorter per-endpoint TTLs for volatile endpoints (dashboard, notifications) instead of a flat 7-day maxAge (PersistentResponseCache.swift:49)
Stop double-caching: pick PersistentResponseCache and set requestCachePolicy accordingly, or shrink URLCache to near-zero (APIClient.swift:65-69)
Extend PersistentResponseCacheTests for key integrity + invalidation

userStories.notes: Networking audit M5/M6/L1. The FNV collision is low-probability/high-impact (multi-tenant leak).

userStories.title: Token-refresh single-flight correctness: fail parked waiters, don't collapse non-401 retries
userStories.description: As a user on a flaky connection, when my access token expires the app's single-flight refresh must propagate the real outcome to every parked request and not misreport unrelated errors as auth failures, so I'm neither logged out spuriously nor left hanging.
acceptanceCriteria: refreshAccessToken parks waiters as Result/typed continuations; on refresh FAILURE all waiters are resumed by throwing (not .resume(returning: Data())) so they do not retry with a dead token (ios/Printyx/Core/Network/APIClient.swift:509-513)
The defer that resumes pendingRequests distinguishes success vs thrown failure (capture outcome, resume accordingly)

401-retry path (APIClient.swift:298-310) re-runs the full status handling for the retry response so a post-refresh 403/404/422/500 surfaces as that error, not APIError.unauthorized, and does not force isAuthenticated=false
A successful authed GET fetched on the post-refresh retry path is written to the response cache
Parked refresh waiters have a bounded wait / cancellation handling so a hung refresh cannot suspend requests indefinitely
Unit tests in ios/PrintyxTests/APIClientTests.swift cover: refresh-failure fails all waiters; post-refresh 500 maps to serverError not unauthorized; concurrent 401s trigger exactly one refresh
userStories.notes: Deep-dive Network audit P1 #1-3,#7. Adjacent to IOS-034 (single-flight existence/terminal-401 keychain clear) but these are the resume-with-wrong-result, error-collapse, no-timeout, and missing-cache-write defects WITHIN the machinery. Verified: defer at APIClient.swift:509-513 resumes waiters with .resume(returning: Data()) on every exit incl. the throws at 516/531. | IMPLEMENTED (pending iOS CI build, IOS-069): refactored APIClient response handling into handleResponse(allowRefresh:) so the 401->refresh->retry path re-runs full status mapping (post-refresh 5xx/4xx surface correctly, GET retry is cached, no refresh loop); refreshAccessToken now fails parked waiters via resume(throwing:) instead of fake resume(returning: Data()). Added 3 APIClientTests (refresh-failure no-retry, post-refresh-500=serverError, concurrent single-flight). Not yet compiled (no macOS/Xcode in this env). | VERIFIED: the 3 new APIClientTests now pass in CI (Build & Test green).

userStories.title: Agentic OS core schema: agent catalog + per-tenant agent settings (kill switch)

Add agent_actions: id, tenant_id, agent_key, action_type, tier smallint (1=auto, 2=human review, 3=human owned), status enum ['proposed','auto_executed','pending_review','approved','rejected','expired','failed'], confidence numeric(5,2), summary text, payload jsonb, result jsonb, idempotency_key varchar unique nullable, review_due_at, reviewed_by, reviewed_at, review_note, correlation_id, created_at, updated_at

userStories.title: Agent guardrail policy schema + typed policy accessor
userStories.description: As a company admin, I need per-tenant guardrail policies (confidence floors, dollar caps, action allowlists, daily action caps) that decide which tier an agent action lands in, so Tier 1 autonomy is bounded by explicit, auditable rules rather than model judgment.
acceptanceCriteria: Add agent_policies to shared/agentic-os-schema.ts: id, tenant_id, agent_key nullable (null = tenant-global), policy_key varchar, value jsonb, updated_by, updated_at, unique(tenant_id, agent_key, policy_key); migration generated

Code defaults exported as AGENT_POLICY_DEFAULTS: confidence_min_auto (0.85), max_auto_dollar_amount (0 = money actions never Tier 1), daily_auto_action_cap (50), business_hours_only (false), tier1_action_allowlist (empty array = allow all non-money actions at agent's default tier)
Unit test server/tests/unit/agentic-policies.test.ts covering precedence (agent > tenant-global > default)
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Explore audit: ai_employees.decision_threshold and task_context guards exist but are NEVER enforced. This table + AOS-010's classifier is the enforcement point. max_auto_dollar_amount=0 default means anything touching money (discounts, refunds, invoice adjustments, dunning sends) starts life as Tier 2 until a tenant explicitly raises it — safe-by-default.

userStories.title: Postgres job queue worker: claim, retry with backoff, dead-letter
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need a durable worker loop that claims agent_jobs safely under concurrency, retries failures with exponential backoff, and dead-letters poison jobs, so agent work is reliable without new infrastructure.
acceptanceCriteria: server/services/agentic/job-queue.ts: enqueueAgentJob(job), claimNextJob(workerId) using SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on (status='queued' AND run_at <= now()) ordered by priority, run_at; sets status='running', locked_at, locked_by
completeJob / failJob: failure increments attempts, re-queues with exponential backoff (run_at = now + 2^attempts minutes) until max_attempts, then status='dead' with last_error
Worker loop started from server bootstrap ONLY when process.env.AGENTIC_OS_ENABLED==='true'; polls every 5s; graceful shutdown on SIGTERM (finish in-flight job, release nothing mid-transaction)
Stale-lock reaper: jobs stuck 'running' with locked_at older than 10 minutes are re-queued (attempt counted)
Unit tests server/tests/unit/agentic-job-queue.test.ts for backoff math and state transitions (db calls mocked)
Typecheck passes: npm run check; tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Runs in the Express process (server/index.ts bootstrap) like cron-service.ts does today — no separate deployment. Job handlers registered by agent_key/job_type map (handlers arrive with each domain agent story). Keep the claim query to raw SQL via db.execute if Drizzle can't express SKIP LOCKED cleanly.

userStories.title: Agent tool registry + executor with Zod validation and tenant pinning
userStories.description: As a security owner, I need agent tools defined in a code registry with schema-validated inputs and context-pinned tenant scope, so an LLM can never fabricate a tool call that crosses tenants or executes something unregistered.

Unit tests: cross-tenant input stripped, invalid input rejected, unknown tool rejected
